paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when people lie about you, you don't have to carry it alone, and you don't have to pretend it doesn't hurt. David says it plainly. People are accusing him in return for his love, and he calls himself "a man of prayer." He doesn't hide the hurt or hand it to the liars. He hands every bit of it to God, and that is what the whole psalm teaches us to do (Psalm 109:4).

Now, that middle part is HEAVY. The prayer asks for hard things, and I think it's raw pain talking. But look where David puts it. He doesn't take revenge into his own hands. He prays it to God and asks that it be "the LORD's reward" (Psalm 109:20). So when you're hurt and angry, bring ALL of it to God, because He can handle what you can't.

Then listen to how the psalm ends. David says, "Though they curse, You will bless," and he promises to thank the LORD "in the presence of many" (Psalm 109:28, 30). The reason is the last verse: "He stands at the right hand of the needy one, to save him from the condemners of his soul." Baker, when the accusing voices are loud, remember who is standing right next to you (Psalm 109:31).
